# Web renderer

`src/web` is a PixiJS renderer that boots the same engine core the Ink terminal
uses, wrapped in a Next.js app shell (`@ts-rogue/web`). It is an independent
drawing layer downstream of `GameStore.subscribe` - it never mutates
`GameState` or reimplements reducer logic.

## Boot + the shared seam

[`bootGame(mount, flags)`](mex://function:de766a85f0f9ec3c8ed7bc936852c519)
builds the initial `GameState`, wires a `GameStore`, initializes the Pixi
`Application` into the mount, builds one container + `SceneChromeView` per scene,
loads the atlas, wires the keyboard manager, and owns the title/game-over
`Phase` on top of the store's scenes. A single `renderCurrent()` redraws from
three triggers: a store dispatch (`subscribe`), the Pixi `resize` event, and
every keydown (menu-cursor moves are local UI state, not `GameEvent`s, so they
would otherwise never redraw). It returns a `dispose()` handle that tears down
every listener + the Pixi app, so React chrome (`app/GamePortal.tsx`) can
mount/unmount it - including StrictMode's double-invoke - without leaking a
second game.

Input is resolved by `input/keyboard.ts`'s `BrowserKeyboardManager` through the
exact same `src/ui/screens/**/interaction.ts` reducers the terminal uses; no
keymap/reducer logic is duplicated here. New player actions are added as a
`GameEvent` + `reduce` case in the engine, not special-cased per renderer.

## Shared framework-free layer

The HUD frame/party-bar/log is built once by [`buildChrome()`](mex://function:3f4d35579ad2237045276b9f87930be2)
(`src/ui/scene/chrome.ts`) as an abstract `PanelNode` tree in `Unit`s - the same
tree the terminal's `Screen.tsx` and this renderer's `render/sceneView.ts`
(`SceneChromeView`) both walk. `UNIT_PX` maps one chrome `Unit` to pixels here.
Every per-scene view (`sceneView`, `battleView`, `dungeonView`, `overworldView`,
`particles`) is framework-free behind a `DrawFactory` interface and unit-tested
without a real WebGL context; a thin `pixi*DrawFactory.ts` adapter supplies real
Pixi objects. Reach for this shared layer before adding renderer-local logic.

## Cross-boundary import guardrails (CI-enforced)

biome (`biome.json` overrides) fails the build on either violation:
- `src/web/**` may not import `ink` or any Node builtin (`node:*`/bare).
- `src/app.tsx` + `src/ui/**` may not import `pixi.js` or touch DOM globals
  (`window`, `document`, `localStorage`).

`pnpm lint` (part of `pnpm check`) runs these on every push. An engine change is
not done until BOTH `pnpm game` and `pnpm web:dev` boot and handle it; `pnpm
web:build` is a separate CI step proving the vite/Next build still succeeds.

## Art pipeline

Full-color 8x8 pixel art from the Minifantasy packs; each atlas frame's source
rect lives in `src/ui/tiles/sources.ts` (`TILE_SOURCES`).
`scripts/build-atlas.ts` packs them into `public/atlas/atlas.png` +
`atlas.json` - **generated, commit both, never hand-edit**. Frames stay native
size; Pixi upscales with `scaleMode = "nearest"`. Battle monsters are separate
individually-loaded textures (`battlers.ts`), not packed into the atlas. The
terminal renderer is pure ASCII and uses none of this. See
`patterns/add-content.md` for adding a sprite.

## Effects are derived, never events

Damage numbers, particle bursts, and hit-flash are derived from state deltas
observed across renders (e.g. a new `"damage"` log entry + an enemy HP drop),
never a new `GameEvent` - the engine stays pure. All effects are additive and
gated on `prefers-reduced-motion` (`setReducedMotion(true)` clears live
particles and stops new ones while legibility features keep rendering).

## Persistence + deployment

Browser save is a single IndexedDB slot (`persistence/browserSave.ts`) sharing
`serializer.ts` with the terminal's `node:sqlite` slot. The app ships as one
Vercel deployment hosting both the game and the eve agent (`next.config.mjs`
wraps config with `withEve`, mounting the agent at `/eve/v1/*`); set the Vercel
project **Root Directory to `src/web`**.

## Verify

- `pnpm web:dev` boots and the changed scene renders correctly (screenshot via
  the play-web harness).
- `pnpm check` (lint catches cross-boundary imports) and `pnpm web:build` pass.
- If an atlas frame changed, `public/atlas/atlas.{png,json}` are regenerated and
  committed.
